Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the OmniRetail Inc. Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for queuing up questions will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to OmniRetail's Q4 2023 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, COO; Riley Patel, CMO; and Casey Nguyen, CTO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of OmniRetail.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q4 performance, driven by robust seasonality trends with peaks in high-intent shopping periods like Black Friday and Cyber Monday, alongside effective strategies to manage deviations through AI forecasting and omnichannel expansions. We saw significant growth in key metrics, including GMV reaching $2.8 billion in Q4, up 28% year-over-year, and full-year GMV at $6.7 billion, a 19% increase.

Our focus remains on expanding gross margins through product mix shifts toward higher-margin categories like home decor and private labels, alongside supply chain efficiencies from owned fulfillment centers and freight optimizations. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our AI recommendation engine, which we believe will significantly boost conversions and average order values.

We are investing heavily in mobile app enhancements and marketing campaigns that drive brand awareness and efficient customer acquisition. We are focused on improving active buyer retention via loyalty programs and personalized experiences. Finally, we are committed to holiday season preparations with optimized inventory levels and demand forecasting to capture projected uplifts.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q4 revenue was $2.8 billion, an increase of 22% year-over-year. Gross margin was 43.2%, driven by product mix shifts to high-margin verticals, private label expansion, and supply chain efficiencies including vertical integration in logistics and AI-optimized inventory management. Operating expenses were $1.2 billion, representing 42% of revenue. Our marketing spend increased 19% year-over-year to $450 million, allocated efficiently across paid search, social commerce, and brand-building, yielding strong ROAS.

Let me dive deeper into some key financial aspects starting with seasonality impact, which is a core cyclical element of our e-commerce model. Peaks align with Black Friday/Cyber Monday, back-to-school, and holidays, where Q4 typically drives 42-45% of annual GMV, focused on apparel, electronics, and home goods comprising 65% of assortments. This Q4, GMV hit $2.8 billion, up 28% YoY, surpassing the 22% industry average per Adobe Analytics, with order volume up 35% to 45 million units and AOV rising 12% to $62 via AI-driven personalized bundling converting 24% of sessions. Full-year GMV was $6.7 billion, up 19%, with Q4 skew at 42%, similar to Amazon's profile.

Deviations included BFCM upside of 15% above guidance at $1.1 billion, from early promotions starting November 15th via Google Shopping and TikTok integrations, mobile conversions at 32%, and PWA optimizations cutting cart abandonment to 65%. Fulfillment costs rose 8% to 14% of GMV but were offset by FlexLogistics with UPS achieving under 2-day delivery for 85% of U.S. orders. Q2 downside of 7% to $1.34 billion stemmed from inflation on big-ticket items, AOV dip to $58, and weather disruptions inflating returns to 22%. Singles Day in APAC beat by 8% at $450 million via live-streaming.

Regionally, North America at 65% of GMV grew 30% but saw high apparel returns at 25%; Europe at 20% grew 12% impacted by energy crises; APAC/LATAM at 15% surged 42% with Pix payments in Brazil lifting AOV 18%. Mitigations include $150 million in AI demand forecasting improving accuracy to 92%, omnichannel BOPIS at 25% of Q4 orders, dynamic pricing for 3% margin uplift, and OmniPrime at 2.1 million subscribers driving 55% of GMV. We're targeting 5-point seasonality reduction by FY25 via groceries and off-peak campaigns. Adjusted EBITDA margins held at 11.2%, Q4 at 15%, with Q1'24 GMV guided at $1.2 billion, full-year 20% growth.

Shifting to gross margin trends, GAAP gross margin expanded 180 basis points YoY to 43.2%, adjusted to 43.7% excluding $15 million in supply chain costs, TTM at 42.8% up from 39.5% in FY2022, gaining 430 basis points since Q2 FY2022 trough. This outperforms Wayfair's 40.1% and ASOS's 41.2%.

Drivers: Product mix to home decor and wellness at 35% of GMV from 22%, with private-label NovaHome at 52% margins vs. 35-38% for electronics; private label at 28% of GMV up from 15%, with NovaEssentials and PureGlow growing 45% YoY; supply chain leverage with owned FCs handling 65% of units cutting costs to $4.50 per unit, freight down 60% to $2,200/FEU, and NovaFlow AI reducing stockouts to 2.1% and markdowns by $45 million.

Regionally, U.S. at 45.1% up 220 bps with returns at 18% via AR try-on; Europe at 39.8% pressured by VAT; APAC/LATAM at 41.5%. Headwinds like promotions clipping 80 bps offset by loyalty pricing; tariffs mitigated by Mexico shift; returns at 20% cut via AI-fit. Outlook: 100-150 bps expansion to 44-45% in FY2025 via scale, NovaOptix AI pricing, APAC private labels, and sustainability credits.

On active buyer growth, our base reached 128 million, up 18% YoY with Q2 acceleration. We added 14.2 million new buyers, up 22%, at CAC of $28 down 12% YoY. Paid social/search at 45% with 4.2x ROAS; affiliates at 28%; organic up 31%. North America 62%, APAC 42%; NovaHunt AI lowered CAC 18%. Retention at 76% up 300 bps, repeats at 4.2 orders, NovaPrime at 42 million members with 8x LTV; churn at 2.1%. Personalization lifts add-to-cart 19%; mobile DAU/MAU 28%. LTV up 24% to $420; Q3 guide 135-138 million.

Our net income for the quarter was $250 million, or $0.85 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of revenue growth at 20% to $12 billion.

Now I'll turn it over to Taylor Kim to discuss operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. Operationally, we focused on supply chain resilience and fulfillment efficiencies, with shipping times improved by 25%. Fulfillment costs were down 22% per unit to $4.50 through owned centers handling 65% of volume. We are implementing AI-optimized inventory via NovaFlow across 95% of top SKUs, reducing days on hand to 42.

On holiday preparations, inventory is at $2.8 billion, up 12% YoY but flat sequentially, optimized for 32% GMV uplift Nov-Jan to $28.5 billion full-year. Electronics $900 million up 18%, apparel $700 million up 8%, home $615 million flat, beauty/toys $485 million. 65% front-loaded in 28 FCs including new Dallas site. Demand from BFCM $4.2 billion +35%, AOV $145 +12%. Electronics +42%, home +28%. North America 62%, EMEA 25%, APAC 13% +45%. ML forecasting at 96% accuracy, JIT with suppliers, eco-packaging 40%. Gross margins 28.5% holiday. Now I'll turn it over to Riley.

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from Back-to-School Blitz and #ShopSphereStyle campaigns on TikTok and Instagram. Customer acquisition costs were $28, down 15% YoY. Our brand awareness increased by 18% in aided recall per Nielsen, unaided to 32%, SOV to 4.2%, EMV $145 million.

Effectiveness shone with 4.2 million net new customers +28%, ROAS 5.8x, performance at 7.2x. Budget 55% search/shopping, 25% social. AI Customer Graph improved targeting 22%; TikTok Shop $120 million; influencers 9x ROAS. North America 2.1 million adds, awareness +20%; Europe 1.1 million; APAC 950K +45%. Challenges like inflation offset by owned channels. Q4 guide 5.5 million adds, CAC <$30, Sphere Rewards 2.0. Now to Casey.

Casey Nguyen:
Thanks, Riley. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI personalization and AR/VR integrations. Our website uptime was 99.9%. Mobile app usage increased by 25% YoY.

Diving into mobile app engagement, we achieved 5.2 million new downloads +28% YoY, cumulative 162 million. ASO on keywords like same-day delivery boosted organic 35%, CPI $1.42 via TikTok. DAU 2.8 million +22%, MAU 18.5 million +25%, DAU/MAU 15.1%, sessions 4.6 per week, retention D1 48%, D30 18%, churn 4.2%. Conversions 9.2% +42% YoY, 68% of GMV $1.47 billion, AOV $58 +12%. Post-v4.2.1 update +19%, summer events +35% DAU. North America iOS 10.4%, Europe Android 8.1%, APAC 7.9%. SwiftAI on-device ML cut latency 40%, AR 18% adoption +22% conv, Passkeys 41%. Targeting 25 million MAU YE'24, app-only verticals.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question and answer session. [Pause] Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On seasonality, could you expand on the Q2 downside and APAC upside deviations, and how AI forecasting mitigates future risks?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Ben. The Q2 softness was macro-driven with inflation hitting appliances down 12%, plus weather impacts raising returns. APAC Singles Day exceeded via live-streaming and FX tailwinds. Our Prophet-Snowflake models boosted accuracy to 92%, cutting stockouts 40%, positioning us well for smoother cycles ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
Strong margins—how sustainable is the 430 bps expansion with promo intensity and tariffs? Regional breakdown?

Jordan Lee:
Great question, Lisa. Mix shift to 52% margin private labels added 110 bps, logistics leverage 250 bps. U.S. 45.1%, Europe 39.8% VAT-hit, APAC 41.5%. Tariffs offset by USMCA Mexico sourcing, promos countered by loyalty AOV. Expect 100-150 bps more via NovaOptix and scale.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Mike Rodriguez:
Holiday inventory at $2.8 billion—risks to demand if consumer softens, and FC expansions?

Taylor Kim:
Mike, solid prep with 42 days inventory via 96% accurate ML at ZIP level, safety buffers 18%. BFCM $4.2 billion expected, diversified sourcing Vietnam/India. New Dallas FC and Rotterdam Q1'25 enhance scalability, monitoring port risks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emma Watson with Barclays.

Emma Watson:
Impressive CAC down 15%—breakdown on TikTok ROAS and influencer impact for acquisition?

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Emma. TikTok Shop up 150% to $120 million, 8.5x ROAS in APAC; influencers 9x via UGC on SphereEssentials. AI Graph and DCO lifted conv 18%, LTV/CAC 4.2x, resilient to ad fatigue with 65% organic.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with RBC Capital Markets.

David Kim:
Mobile conv at 9.2%—tech behind AR try-on adoption and APAC Android strategy?

Casey Nguyen:
David, AR/VR on 5,000 SKUs sees 18% sessions +22% conv; SwiftAI on-device for feeds cut latency 40%. APAC Android 85% share, UPI/Hindi support for 1.2 million MAU India, sub-2s loads on GraphQL targeting Amazon-like 12%.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Active buyer count growth: User acquisition and retention rates.
Effectiveness of marketing campaigns: Brand awareness and customer acquisition.
